claim: Sox9-CreER specifically labels hair follicle epithelial cells including HFSCs, but not McSCs when tamoxifen is administered from postnatal day 1 to 4.
source: Tamoxifen treatment from postnatal (P) day 1 to 4 results in specific labeling of HF epithelial cells including the HFSCs, but not the McSCs (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence imaging data showing RFP+ labeling pattern in Sox9-CreER::Ai14 mice

claim: RBP-J is efficiently ablated in HF epithelial cells of Sox9-CreER::Rbpj cKO mice at first telogen.
source: Efficient RBP-J ablation by Sox9-CreER::Rbpj <fl/fl> in HF epithelial cells was confirmed by RBP-J staining at the first telogen (Figure 1B).
evidence: Confirmed by immunofluorescence staining showing loss of RBP-J protein in CD34+ HFSCs

claim: Loss of RBP-J in HF epithelial cells does not immediately affect HFSC markers CD34 and Sox9 expression.
source: Loss of RBP-J in HF epithelial cells does not lead to immediate loss of HFSC markers CD34 and Sox9 (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), nor does the overall morphology of the telogen bulge change.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing maintained expression of CD34 and Sox9 in cKO bulge

claim: Sox9-CreER::RBP-J cKO HFs show ectopic pigmentation in the bulge region at the telogen to anagen transition stage.
source: But unexpectedly, we noticed the bulge region in the Sox9-CreER::RBP-J cKO HFs show ectopic pigmentation at the telogen to anagen transition stage, which is not observed in the WT HFs (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Demonstrated by Masson-Fontana melanin staining showing pigmentation in bulge region

claim: More than 60% of Sox9-CreER::RBP-J cKO HFs show ectopic pigmentation in the bulge at telogen to anagen transition, increasing to about 90% in early anagen.
source: Based on melanin specific Masson-Fontana staining and quantification, more than 60% of the Sox9-CreER::RBP-J cKO HFs start to show ectopic pigmentation in the bulge region at telogen to anagen transition stage. This is even more obvious in early anagen when about 90% of the bulge become pigmented, in comparison less than 20% of the WT HFs show pigmentation in the bulge region (Figure 1C).
evidence: Quantified from melanin staining across multiple follicles and mice

claim: RBP-J is required for HFSC downstream progenies terminal differentiation.
source: This is consistent with previous publication that as the main co-factor of the canonical Notch pathway RBP-J is required for HFSC downstream progenies terminal differentiation (Demehri and Kopan, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous publication

claim: Krt6-CreER was generated by inserting IRES-CreER cassette after Krt6a exon9 using CRISPR/Cas9.
source: To this end, we used CRISPR/Cas9 to insert the IRES-CreER cassette after the Krt6a exon9 (Figure 2A).
evidence: Described methodology with schematic diagram showing insertion strategy

claim: Krt6-CreER labels CD34+ HFSCs and Krt6+ companion layer cells in close to 100% of HFs, but only less than 10% of HFs contain occasionally labeled cells in the sHG when tamoxifen is injected during second telogen.
source: When tamoxifen was injected during the second telogen, we found that CD34+ HFSCs and Krt6+ companion layer cells (CPL) are efficiently labeled in close to 100% of the HFs, but only less than 10% of HFs contain occasionally labeled cells in the sHG (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Quantified from immunofluorescence imaging of Krt6-CreER::Ai6 mice

claim: Approximately 80% of HFSCs in dorsal skin are labeled using the Krt6-CreER line.
source: FACS analysis indicates that ~80% of HFSCs in dorsal skin are labeled using our Krt6-CreER line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Quantified by FACS analysis of GFP+ cells within CD34+, integrin-α6+ HFSC population

claim: RBP-J is efficiently ablated in both HFSCs and CPL cells but not sHG cells in Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO mice at telogen.
source: Restricted loss of RBP-J in HFSCs and CPL cells but not sHG cells was confirmed by RBP-J staining at telogen (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Confirmed by immunofluorescence staining showing loss of RBP-J in bulge but not sHG

claim: In anagen follicles of Krt6-CreER::RBP-J mice, cells in the lower HF generated by telogen sHG cells are RBP-J positive, while upper HF bulge cells are RBP-J negative.
source: When cKO follicles enter anagen, cells in the lower HF generated by telogen sHGs cells are all RBP-J positive, while the upper HF bulge cells are all RBP-J negative (Figure 2D).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing differential RBP-J expression pattern in anagen HF

claim: McSCs do not express Krt6.
source: McSCs do not express Krt6 and the number of McSCs in the bulge and their downstream progenies located in the bulb of anagen HFs are normal following telogen cKO of RBP-J in Krt6-CreER::RBP-J mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Inferred from labeling specificity and McSC quantification data

claim: The number of McSCs in the bulge and their downstream progenies in the bulb are normal in Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO mice.
source: McSCs do not express Krt6 and the number of McSCs in the bulge and their downstream progenies located in the bulb of anagen HFs are normal following telogen cKO of RBP-J in Krt6-CreER::RBP-J mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Quantified by counting DCT+ cells in bulge and bulb regions

claim: Wax removal of hair follicles at telogen removes club hair and attached Krt6+ CPL cells but not HFSCs.
source: HF wax at telogen only removes the club hair and the attached Krt6+ CPL cells but not the HFSCs (Figure 2F).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing presence of CD34+ HFSCs but absence of Krt6+ CPL cells after wax

claim: Removal of CPL cells at telogen triggers anagen entry.
source: Removal of CPL cells at telogen also triggers anagen entry (Chen et al., 2012) (Figure 2G).
evidence: Supported by citation and demonstrated by morphological changes after wax

claim: Cell apoptosis and proliferation are the same in bulge area between WT and Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO follicles.
source: Cell apoptosis and proliferation are the same in bulge area between WT and cKO follicles (Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: Quantified by cleaved-Caspase3 and Ki67 staining

claim: After wax-induced anagen entry, 90% of Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO HFs show ectopic pigmentation in bulge at D3 post wax, compared to less than 20% of WT HFs.
source: Starting at D3 post wax, 90% of the cKO HFs contain pigmented bulge, compared to less than 20% of WT HFs with the same phenomenon (Figure 2I).
evidence: Quantified from Masson-Fontana melanin staining

claim: Increased Tyrp1 levels are detected in McSCs of Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO HFs starting at D2 post wax when HFs are still in telogen.
source: We also detect increased Tyrp1 levels in McSCs of the cKO HFs starting at D2 post wax when the HFs are still in telogen, while in WT HFs the expression of Tyrp1 is restricted to differentiated melanocytes located in the bulb of anagen HFs (Figure 2J).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing Tyrp1 expression in DCT+ McSCs in bulge

claim: McSCs are influenced in a paracrine fashion by loss of RBP-J specifically in HFSCs.
source: Since the phenotype occurs after removal of the CPL cells, we conclude that McSCs are influenced in a paracrine fashion by loss of RBP-J specifically in HFSC.
evidence: Inferred from persistence of phenotype after CPL removal, leaving only HFSCs as RBP-J null cells

claim: HFSCs play an essential role in maintaining a differentiation refractory niche environment for neighboring McSCs.
source: It reveals an essential role of HFSCs in maintaining a differentiation refractory niche environment for the neighboring McSCs.
evidence: Inferred from the ectopic differentiation of McSCs when RBP-J is lost in HFSCs

claim: RBP-J is expressed by most cells in HFs from the beginning of morphogenesis to adult telogen.
source: We found RBP-J is expressed by most cells in HFs from the beginning of morphogenesis to adult telogen (Figure 3A).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing broad RBP-J expression pattern across hair cycle stages

claim: The active form of Notch1 ICD (N1ICD) is only detected in terminally differentiated cells in the pre-cortex of anagen HFs or CPL cells in telogen HFs, but not in HFSCs.
source: In contrast, the active form of Notch1 ICD (N1ICD) is only detected in the terminally differentiated cells in the pre-cortex cells of anagen HFs or CPL cells in telogen HFs, but not in the HFSCs (Figure 3B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing restricted N1ICD expression pattern

claim: N1ICD and N2ICD are expressed at low or undetectable levels in HFSCs compared to high levels in matrix cells.
source: Western blot analysis of these sorted cells revealed little or no expression of N1ICD and N2ICD in the HFSCs, compared to high level of these two proteins in the matrix cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis of FACS-isolated HFSCs and matrix cells

claim: N3ICD is not detected in either HFSCs or matrix cells.
source: No N3ICD was detected in either cell population.
evidence: Stated based on Western blot analysis

claim: Canonical Notch downstream target genes Hes1 and Hey1 are expressed at much lower levels in HFSCs compared to differentiated matrix cells.
source: We then checked the expression pattern of canonical Notch downstream target genes Hes1 and Hey1 using qPCR. Consistent with our western blot results, they are much lower in HFSCs compared to differentiated matrix cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis of FACS-isolated cells

claim: Active Notch receptor ICDs and canonical Notch downstream targets are lower in HFSCs compared to differentiated CPL cells in telogen HFs.
source: Similarly, active Notch receptor ICDs and canonical Notch downstream targets are lower in HFSCs compared to the differentiated CPL cells (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot and qPCR analysis of FACS-isolated telogen cells

claim: Active Notch signaling is absent in HFSCs and RBP-J serves as a repressor in them.
source: All these results indicate active Notch signaling is absent in HFSCs and RBP-J serves as a repressor in them.
evidence: Inferred from low levels of Notch ICDs and downstream targets in HFSCs

claim: Retinoid metabolic process genes are upregulated in Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO HFSCs compared to WT.
source: Finally our GO_BP analysis revealed retinoid metabolic process genes as an unexpected category up regulated in cKO HFSCs compared to WT (Figure 3G).
evidence: Identified through Gene Ontology analysis of RNA-seq data

claim: Gene set enrichment analysis shows differences in retinoid metabolic process related genes between WT and cKO HFSCs.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis also showed differences in retinoid metabolic process related genes between WT and cKO HFSCs (Figure 3H).
evidence: Demonstrated by GSEA analysis of RNA-seq data

claim: Retinoid metabolic process genes ADH1, RBP2 and RDH1 are expressed at 3-4 fold higher levels in HFSCs from Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO compared to WT HFs.
source: This result is confirmed by qPCR using FACS isolated HFSCs from cKO and WT telogen skin. Retinoid metabolic process genes such as ADH1, RBP2 and RDH1 are expressed at 3 ~ 4 fold higher in HFSCs from Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO compared to WT HFs (Figure 3I).
evidence: Confirmed by qPCR analysis of FACS-isolated HFSCs

claim: RA downstream genes Cdkn1a, Crabp2, Hbegf, and Lefty are statistically significantly higher in RBP-J cKO compared to WT HFSCs.
source: We found that even though McSC markers such as DCT and c-Kit levels were similar in all four groups examined, melanocyte lineage master regulator MITF and melanocyte differentiation marker Tyrp1 was significantly down regulated in McSCs isolated from cKO HFs after RA synthesis inhibitor WIN18446 treatment, consistent with the ectopic pigmentation change.
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis of FACS-isolated HFSCs

claim: WT HFs contain approximately 50 pg RA per million HFSCs, while cKO HFs contain approximately 90 pg RA per million HFSCs.
source: We also measured the level of RA directly using ELISA assay. WT HFs contain ~50 pg RA per million HFSCs, while the cKO HFs contain ~90 pg RA per million HFSCs (Figure 5B).
evidence: Measured by ELISA assay using FACS-isolated HFSCs

claim: RBP-J functions as a repressor in HFSCs to suppress retinoid metabolic process genes and consequently the level of RA in the niche shared by HFSCs and McSCs.
source: These results revealed that RBP-J functions as a repressor in HFSCs to suppress retinoid metabolic process genes and consequently the level of RA in the niche shared by HFSCs and McSCs.
evidence: Inferred from upregulation of retinoid genes and increased RA levels upon RBP-J loss

claim: About 6000 out of 95,000 ATAC-seq peaks were more accessible in cKO HFSCs compared to WT HFSCs.
source: About 6000 in 95,000 peaks were more accessible in cKO HFSCs compared to WT HFSCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: Quantified from ATAC-seq analysis

claim: Regions with more accessibility in cKO HFSCs compared to WT were enriched for promoter regions.
source: In contrast, regions with more accessibility in cKO HFSCs compared to WT were enriched for promoter, which fits putative RBP-J binding regions (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: Demonstrated by genomic classification analysis of ATAC-seq peaks

claim: The promoters and 5'-UTRs of Hes1, Krt10, and Adh1 were more accessible in cKO HFSCs compared to WT.
source: We found for canonical Notch signal downstream gene Hes1, keratinocyte differentiation gene Krt10, and retinoid metabolic process gene Adh1, their promoters and 5' -UTRs were more accessible in cKO HFSCs compared to WT (Figure 4D).
evidence: Demonstrated by ATAC-seq track signals at specific loci

claim: DNA regions with changed accessibility overlap with putative RBP-J binding motifs.
source: The DNA regions that demonstrate changed accessibility also overlap with putative RBP-J binding motif based on published RBP-J CHIP-seq analysis (Meredith et al., 2013; Castel et al., 2013).
evidence: Compared with published ChIP-seq data

claim: Overexpression of RBP-J significantly decreases Adh1 promoter driven luciferase level.
source: We found overexpression of RBP-J significantly decreased the relative Adh1 promoter driven luciferase level, but co-transfection of both RBP-J and N1ICD increased the relative Adh1 promoter driven luciferase level (Figure 4F).
evidence: Demonstrated by in vitro luciferase reporter assay

claim: Co-transfection of both RBP-J and N1ICD increases Adh1 promoter driven luciferase level.
source: We found overexpression of RBP-J significantly decreased the relative Adh1 promoter driven luciferase level, but co-transfection of both RBP-J and N1ICD increased the relative Adh1 promoter driven luciferase level (Figure 4F).
evidence: Demonstrated by in vitro luciferase reporter assay

claim: After RBP-J ablation, the chromatin states of some RBP-J targeted genes became more open and resulted in higher transcriptional activity.
source: Taken together, after RBP-J ablation, the chromatin states of some RBP-J targeted genes were changed and became more open and resulted in higher transcriptional activity.
evidence: Inferred from ATAC-seq and gene expression data

claim: RA synthesis inhibitor WIN18446 treatment decreases RA level in cKO HFs from approximately 90 pg to approximately 30 pg RA per million HFSCs.
source: After treatment, RA level in cKO HFs was decreased from ~90 pg RA per million HFSCs to ~30 pg RA per million HFSCs, as measured by ELISA assay using FACS isolated HFSCs (Figure 5B).
evidence: Measured by ELISA assay

claim: Ectopic pigmentation in cKO bulge is efficiently rescued by WIN18446 treatment.
source: The ectopic pigmentation in cKO bulge was efficiently rescued by WIN18446 treatment, but not vehicle treatment (Figure 5C).
evidence: Demonstrated by Masson-Fontana staining showing reduced pigmentation after treatment

claim: After WIN18446 treatment, only about 20% of cKO HFs show ectopic pigmentation in the bulge, compared to approximately 80% without treatment.
source: Compared to ~80% of cKO HFs showing ectopic pigmentation in the bulge, only about 20% of cKO HFs did after treatment with WIN18446.
evidence: Quantified from Masson-Fontana staining

claim: MITF and Tyrp1 are significantly down regulated in McSCs isolated from cKO HFs after RA synthesis inhibitor WIN18446 treatment.
source: We found that even though McSC markers such as DCT and c-Kit levels were similar in all four groups examined, melanocyte lineage master regulator MITF and melanocyte differentiation marker Tyrp1 was significantly down regulated in McSCs isolated from cKO HFs after RA synthesis inhibitor WIN18446 treatment, consistent with the ectopic pigmentation change.
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis of FACS-isolated McSCs

claim: RA is necessary to induce ectopic McSC differentiation in the aberrant niche of Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO HFs.
source: This result revealed that RA is necessary to induce ectopic McSC differentiation in the aberrant niche of Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO HFs.
evidence: Inferred from rescue of phenotype by RA synthesis inhibitor

claim: Topical RA treatment at 2 nM to 200 nM dosage results in approximately 50% of dorsal skin HFs showing ectopic pigmentation in the bulge at D4 after wax.
source: At 2 nM ~200 nM RA dosage,~50% of dorsal skin HFs show ectopic pigmentation in the bulge at D4 after wax.
evidence: Quantified from Masson-Fontana staining after topical RA treatment

claim: At 6 hr timepoint, 1 to 100 nM RA is sufficient to induce higher c-Kit and Tyrp1 levels in cultured primary McSCs, but at 12 hr timepoint this induction is diminished.
source: We found that at 6 hr timepoint, 1 to 100 nM RA is sufficient to induce higher c-Kit and Tyrp1 level but at 12 hr timepoint, this induction is diminished (Figure 5F).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis of cultured primary McSCs treated with RA

claim: RA can induce McSCs differentiation in a time and dosage dependent manner.
source: This demonstrates RA can induce McSCs differentiation in a time and dosage dependent manner.
evidence: Inferred from in vitro and in vivo RA treatment experiments

claim: Elevated level of RA is both necessary and sufficient to induce ectopic McSC pigmentation in the niche in hair cycle dependent fashion.
source: Together these results indicate that elevated level of RA is both necessary and sufficient to induce ectopic McSC pigmentation in the niche in hair cycle dependent fashion.
evidence: Inferred from RA inhibitor rescue and RA treatment experiments

claim: The percentage of c-Kithigh cells among c-Kit+ cells increased 2-fold in Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO and Sox9-CreER::RBP-J cKO mice compared to WT.
source: We found that although percentage of total c-Kit+ McSC is not changed (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), the percentage of c-Kithigh cells among the c-Kit+ cells increased 2-fold in the Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO and Sox9-CreER::RBP-J cKO mice compared to WT (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Quantified by FACS analysis

claim: RA can increase c-Kit protein level by influencing its translation in testes tissue.
source: It has been reported that RA can increase c-Kit protein level by influencing its translation in testes tissue (Busada et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from previous publication

claim: After WIN18446 treatment, the increased percentage of c-Kithigh/c-Kit+ from Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO skin was dramatically decreased to level slightly lower than WT.
source: After WIN18446 treatment, the percentage of c-Kithigh/c-Kit+ did not change in WT skin, but the increased percentage of c-Kithigh/c-Kit+ from Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO skin was dramatically decreased to level slightly lower than WT (Figure 6A).
evidence: Quantified by FACS analysis after RA synthesis inhibitor treatment

claim: Topical RA treatment significantly increases c-Kit RFI (Relative Fluorescence Intensity) in vivo.
source: In vivo, we quantified c-Kit RFI(Relative Fluorescence Intensity) by immunofluorescence after topical RA treatment and found significant increase (Figure 6B).
evidence: Quantified by immunofluorescence imaging

claim: The c-Kit mRNA levels are similar in FACS isolated McSCs from WT and Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO skin.
source: The effect of RA on c-Kit level in vivo was not due to change in transcription level because based on our qPCR result, the c-Kit mRNA levels were similar in FACS isolated McSCs from WT and Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO skin (Figure 5D).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis

claim: When c-Kit 5'UTR-GFP fusion protein is over-expressed with RA receptor RARα in 293t cells, GFP level is repressed, and this repression can be released when 1 μM RA is added.
source: Mechanistically we found that when we over-expressed c-Kit 5'UTR-GFP fusion protein under the control ubiquitous promoter CMV in 293 t cells, GFP level is repressed if we co-expressed RA receptor RARα, and this repression can be released when 1 μM RA is added into the medium (Figure 6C) (Poon and Chen, 2008).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis of in vitro transfection experiment

claim: Overexpression of c-Kit in cultured primary melanocytes results in about two fold increase in Tyrp1 mRNA level in the presence of KIT-ligand SCF.
source: In the presence of ligand, overexpression of c-Kit in melanocytes resulted in about two fold increase in the Tyrp1 mRNA level, which is similar to the level of increase observed in the FACS isolated McSCs from cKO skin.
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis of cultured melanocytes

claim: Increased level of RA from RBP-J null HFSCs leads to increased level of c-Kit protein on McSCs and ectopic pigmentation phenotype in the mutant niche.
source: Taken together, these results show that increased level of RA from the RBP-J null HFSCs leads to increased level of c-Kit protein on McSCs and the ectopic pigmentation phenotype in the mutant niche.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experiments showing RA effects on c-Kit and differentiation

claim: SCF expression is detected in HFSCs at both telogen and anagen stages with no difference between WT and Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO.
source: First we did qPCR analysis of KIT-ligand SCF in FACS isolated HFSCs from WT and Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO dorsal skin at both telogen and anagen. At both hair cycle stages we did detect SCF expression in the HFSCs but there was no difference between the WT and cKO.
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis of FACS-isolated HFSCs

claim: When HFSCs transition from telogen to anagen, there are significant increases in the level of SCF mRNA in both WT and cKO.
source: However, when HFSCs transitioned from telogen to anagen, there were significant increase in the level of SCF mRNA in both WT and cKO (Figure 7C).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis comparing telogen and anagen HFSCs

claim: Krt6-CreER::RBP-J::SCF cKO completely rescues the McSC ectopic differentiation phenotype in the bulge area without affecting terminal differentiation of melanocytes in the matrix.
source: When compared to Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO, the Krt6-CreER::RBP-J::SCF cKO completely rescued the McSC ectopic differentiation phenotype in the bulge area without affecting terminal differentiation of melanocytes in the matrix (Figure 7D).
evidence: Demonstrated by Masson-Fontana staining showing rescue of bulge pigmentation

claim: The expression of melanocyte differentiation marker Tyrp1 is down regulated in Krt6-CreER::RBP-J::SCF cKO HFs.
source: Furthermore, the expression of melanocyte differentiation marker Tyrp1 was also down regulated in the Krt6-CreER::RBP-J::SCF cKO HFs (Figure 7E).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing reduced Tyrp1 in McSCs

claim: KIT-ligand originated from HFSCs activates the c-Kit-MEK pathway to induce McSC ectopic differentiation in the mutant niche.
source: This genetic rescue experiment confirms that it is the KIT-ligand originated from HFSCs that activates the c-Kit-MEK pathway to induce McSC ectopic differentiation in the mutant niche.
evidence: Inferred from genetic rescue by SCF deletion

claim: The level of KIT-ligand SCF in HFSCs is not changed between WT and Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO skin.
source: It's worth emphasize that the level of KIT-ligand SCF in HFSCs was not changed between WT and Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO skin (Figure 7C).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis

claim: McSCs maintain self-renewal ability by expressing low level of c-Kit to remain insensitive to differentiation signals.
source: So this striking rescue effect by ablation of SCF revealed that the McSCs niche environment is not devoid of differentiation signals. McSC maintain self-renewal ability by expressing low level of c-Kit to remain insensitive to the differentiation signals.
evidence: Inferred from genetic rescue and c-Kit level data

claim: HFSCs actively suppress differentiation-sensitizing signals such as RA level in the niche to help maintain a differentiation refractory niche environment.
source: While their neighboring HFSCs are not just passive receiver of signaling inputs from the niche, they actively suppress differentiation-sensitizing signals in the niche, such as RA level, to help maintain a differentiation refractory niche environment (Figure 7F).
evidence: Inferred from the role of RBP-J in suppressing RA metabolism

claim: Higher MEK downstream pERK signaling is observed in McSCs in cKO follicles.
source: On the other hand, we observed higher MEK downstream pERK signaling in McSCs in cKO follicles (Figure 7A), and also found treatment of MEK pathway inhibitor PD0325901 efficiently rescued the ectopic pigmentation phenotype in mutant skin (Figure 7B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing increased pERK in McSCs

claim: Treatment of MEK pathway inhibitor PD0325901 efficiently rescues the ectopic pigmentation phenotype in mutant skin.
source: On the other hand, we observed higher MEK downstream pERK signaling in McSCs in cKO follicles (Figure 7A), and also found treatment of MEK pathway inhibitor PD0325901 efficiently rescued the ectopic pigmentation phenotype in mutant skin (Figure 7B).
evidence: Demonstrated by Masson-Fontana staining showing reduced pigmentation after treatment

claim: The mTOR pathway inhibitor rapamycin can effectively arrest HFs in telogen.
source: The mTOR pathway inhibitor rapamycin can effectively arrest HFs in telogen as reported before (Kellenberger and Tauchi, 2013).
evidence: Cited from previous publication

claim: Ectopic pigmentation phenotype persists in Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO bulge after rapamycin treatment.
source: But the ectopic pigmentation phenotype still persisted in Krt6-CreER::RBP-J cKO bulge after rapamycin treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by Masson-Fontana staining

claim: The increased level of c-Kit on McSCs is required for ectopic differentiation of McSCs via the c-Kit-MEK pathway.
source: So, together these results confirmed that the increased level of c-Kit on McSCs is required for the ectopic differentiation of McSCs via the c-Kit-MEK pathway.
evidence: Inferred from MEK inhibitor rescue and pERK signaling data

claim: PD0325901 treatment can significantly diminish the differentiation of melanocytes in the matrix of anagen HFs.
source: Notably, the PD0325901 treat can also significantly diminish the differentiation of melanocyte in the matrix of anagen HFs, which is consistent with the known function of c-Kit for melanocyte terminal differentiation (Ito et al., 1999).
evidence: Observed in staining data and consistent with cited literature

claim: Under RA concentration (1 μg) similar to daily use (1-5 μg), there is no obvious difference in McSC number compared to vehicle group.
source: We found that under concentration (1 μg) similar to daily use (1 ~ 5 μg), there is no obvious difference of McSC number comparing to vehicle group, which means RA is safe and will not lead to McSC loss during our daily care.
evidence: Quantified from McSC counts after topical RA treatment

claim: Treatment with lower concentration of RA (1 ng) results in a slight but significant increase in McSC number.
source: Interestingly, when we treated with lower concentration (1 ng), there is a slight but significant increase in McSC number.
evidence: Quantified from McSC counts after topical RA treatment

claim: Nfib expression is the same in control and cKO HFSCs based on RNA-seq data.
source: In our RNA-seq, Nfib expression is the same in Ctrl and cKO HFSCs (232.198 v.s. 203.073).
evidence: Stated based on RNA-seq FPKM values

claim: Edn family genes are either not expressed or show decreased expression in cKO HFSCs.
source: Edn family genes are either not expressed or shows decreased expression in cKO HFSCs. (Edn1: 0.237 v.s. 0.155; Edn2: 4.10 v.s. 1.75; Edn3: 0.073 v.s. 0).
evidence: Stated based on RNA-seq FPKM values

claim: Metabolites represent an entirely new realm of signaling molecules that mediate SC and niche cross talk.
source: Besides the well-studied morphogens, we discover that metabolites represent an entirely new realm of signaling molecules that mediates SC and niche cross talk, and their potential functions warrant further studies in the other systems under homeostasis and pathological conditions.
evidence: Inferred from the discovery that RA mediates HFSC-McSC crosstalk

claim: The niche shared by HFSCs and McSCs is not devoid of differentiation signal.
source: Unexpectedly, we found here that the niche shared by HFSCS and McSCs is not devoid of differentiation signal.
evidence: Inferred from presence of SCF in the niche

claim: HFSCs secreted KIT-ligand is sufficient to induce differentiation of neighboring McSCs when c-Kit protein level on McSCs is elevated by increased RA levels.
source: In fact the HFSCs secreted KIT-ligand is sufficient to induce the differentiation of neighboring McSCs in the niche, when the c-Kit protein level on McSCs is elevated by increased RA levels in the niche.
evidence: Inferred from genetic rescue by SCF deletion and RA effects on c-Kit

claim: During normal homeostasis, the Notch pathway co-factor RBP-J functions in HFSCs to suppress retinoid metabolic process genes.
source: During normal homeostasis, the Notch pathway co-factor RBP-J functions in HFSCs to suppress the retinoid metabolic process genes.
evidence: Demonstrated by upregulation of retinoid genes upon RBP-J loss

claim: HFSCs play an instructive role in maintaining a differentiation refractory niche environment for neighboring McSCs.
source: This reveals that HFSCs play an instructive role in maintaining a differentiation refractory niche environment for the neighboring McSCs.
evidence: Inferred from the role of HFSCs in regulating RA levels
